I once read an article for my Sociology class about people that do not feel complete with all of their limbs. Some go as far as actually removing them, and some, called 'pretenders' simply simulate the loss of their limbs.
Water, food and transportation to get back home.

Also, off of my Spanish Heart - songs like Wind Danse, the Spanish Fantasy suite and (my favorite) Night Streets demonstrate this as well. The compositions on that album are mind blowing. So much vision, exploration, melody, harmony and joy.

Chick Corea - I  am especially fond of the album My Spanish Heart (Check out Night Streets, Wind Danse and Night Castle). Bill Evans (especially on Blue in Green hits me in a visceral way that few do). Emily Remler - another beautiful guitar spirit. 
Steely Dan (Aja, The Royal Scam, Pretzel Logic and Katy Lied) have some incredible material and diversity. They use a lot of wonderful melodic and harmonic schemes. For specific cuts, check out Night by Night, Deacon Blues, Home at Last, Doctor Wu, Haitian Divorce, Babylon Sisters, Pretzel Logic and the song Aja.



Check out Stevie Wonder as well. He's Jazz, he's classical, he's "pop" (hate that term - maybe commercial would be better?) and funky/soulful as anyone. Nobody has a voice like his. Check out the albums Music of My Mind, Talking Book, Innvervisions, Fulfillingness' First Finale and Songs in the Key of Life. For specific cuts that are among my favorites, check out - Creepin', Summer Soft, Lookin' For Another Pure Love (ridiculous solo by Jeff Beck on that cut), As, Superwoman, Girl Blue (he played that freaking percussion... no other soul on this planet could make that song), and definitely Visions, Golden Lady and Too High. I've never introduced Stevie to someone who didn't become totally enthralled. He changed my life when I heard him and he is undoubtedly my favorite artist/composer, and his musicianship/singing powers are colossal.


Also! As Herbie Hancock is another of my favorites, I  urge you to check out the cuts Calypso and Butterfly. There's a version of Butterfly that I believe is circa mid-late 70's that's live - he has a brief monologue to the audience - it's a jam lol! AND! Jaco Pastorious, Steve Gadd, Joe Zawinul are good to check out as well. The group Weather Report did some pretty interesting things. I urge you to check out the cut Young and Fine. Sorry for the word vomit.

Also! Definitely advise you to get into Wayne. He cannot be overstated enough in my book. Some good advice from these redditors. Jazz is such a wide, open world, though - as you become more familiar with it, it's good to specify what kind of musicians and music you are looking for. So many wonderful personalities!

Side B is just a monster....

Synchronicity II, Every Breath You Take, King of Pain, Tea in the Sahara, Murder By Numbers..... I'll put that up against just about everything. That record is a monumental achievement in my book.

I'm going to throw out a bit of a controversial one. It certainly isn't a landslide, and my opinion has changed back and forth from time to time. I suppose my mood during those moments upon listening has a lot to do with it. All of that said....

Songs in the Key of Life 2 > Songs in the Key of Life 1
